clue.text: Regular guy's brief task wielding pickaxes

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, so the last letter of the job word is lopped off

parts.note: a task is a job

indicators.note: wielding pickaxes means swinging them about, so their letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A labourer's short shift of swinging pickaxes, the picture of a regular working man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts JOB to JO; 'wielding' rearranges PICKAXES into ESIXPACK.
explanation.definitionFit: An American slang name for the typical ordinary working-class man, someone with a six-pack of beer.

clue.text: Full of energy, Yank's brief catcall

indicators.note: a container that is full of something holds it, so the shortened word wraps round the energy letter
brief means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to yank is to jerk
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An American, bursting with vigour, gives a short whistle at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb to jerk; 'brief' trims JERK to JER, which is 'Full of' E.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcall is a derisive shout, and a jeer is a mocking cry of the same kind.

clue.text: Virgin turned up before boy made a scene

indicators.note: the reversed word comes before the boy in the answer
in a down answer, a word turned up is written from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: virgin means pure, untouched
Ted is a common boy's name

explanation.surface: A virgin arrived ahead of a boy, causing a public fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'turned up' means written upwards, so the word reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To erupt is to burst out angrily, which is what someone making a scene does.

clue.text: One affecting less classy taste made good in French society?

definitions.text: One affecting less classy taste made good in French society?

parts.words: One affecting less classy taste made good in French society?
parts.note: someone who scorns refinement; read as an instruction, the answer turns a four-letter word for a social climber backwards, giving bon, French for good, plus S for society

explanation.surface: A social climber who made good in high French society.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works as an instruction: SNOB turned backwards gives BON (good in French) + S (society). The question mark is the only signal for this reverse reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person looks down on refinement and makes a show of preferring working-class or unpretentious tastes.

clue.text: Advice not to print sermon here

definitions.meaning: telling someone to pulp the text, destroying the paper rather than publishing it
the raised enclosed platform in a church where a preacher delivers the address

explanation.walkthrough: Split as PULP IT, the answer is an instruction to destroy a manuscript instead of printing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's raised preaching stand is where a sermon is delivered; read as two words it tells an editor to scrap the copy.

clue.text: A very long time to bed in a plant

indicators.note: to bed something in is to set it firmly inside, so the A is planted within the long period

parts.note: a century is a hundred years, a very long time

explanation.surface: A gardener's note that a plant will take ages to bed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bed in' puts A inside CENTURY.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaury is a small pink-flowered wild plant of the gentian family.

clue.text: Wife beginning to cheer for dessert

parts.note: a cheer begins 'hip, hip, hooray', so its opening word is hip

explanation.surface: A wife starts cheering when the pudding arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to cheer' is not the letter C: it is the first word of the cheer 'hip, hip, hooray'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip is a light dessert made with whipped cream or egg whites and fruit.

clue.text: The underworld nearly freezes, making twisted shapes

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: hell is the underworld
ices means freezes

explanation.surface: Hell nearly freezing over, the proverbial sign of something impossible, makes contorted forms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims HELL to HEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Helices are spirals or corkscrew forms, the plural of helix.

clue.text: Wheezily make it over the line, having snacked in this case?

parts.note: to puff past is to get by something while wheezing for breath
RY, short for railway, is a crossword line

explanation.surface: A runner who ate before the race wheezes across the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the line' is not the finishing line but a railway line, abbreviated RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaky layered dough is what you might have eaten in a snack such as a sausage roll; the question mark flags this loose description.

clue.text: Vital queen moves, or one as good

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are moved around, as chess pieces move

explanation.surface: A chess remark that the queen's moves are vital, or something just as good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges VITAL QUEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An equal in worth or value is something that is just as good.

clue.text: Character on staff nearly broken

indicators.note: nearly means almost all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: cleft means split or broken

explanation.surface: A staff member's personality nearly broken by work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is not employees but the musical stave; 'nearly' trims CLEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical symbol written at the start of the stave, fixing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: How your cohort tries to make you take a close look?

definitions.text: How your cohort tries to make you take a close look?

parts.words: How your cohort tries to make you take a close look?
parts.note: the influence of your contemporaries pushing you to conform, punningly read as pressure to scrutinise closely

explanation.walkthrough: Peer means both an equal in your group and to look closely; the clue plays on the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The social influence a group of contemporaries exerts to make someone conform, here read as urging someone to squint.

clue.text: Silly fuss put to Americans to resolve

indicators.note: to resolve something is to break it down and sort it out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trivial dispute is referred to the Americans to settle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to resolve' rearranges PUT TO AMERICANS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a great commotion over something trivial.

clue.text: In composing letter, I may follow yours without variation

definitions.text: In composing letter, I may follow yours
definitions.meaning: a formal letter is signed off 'Yours' followed by this word

explanation.walkthrough: In British letter-writing convention, a letter opening 'Dear Sir' closes with this word after 'Yours'.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard sign-off of a formal letter, and also an adverb meaning exactly, with complete accuracy.

clue.text: Again gets in GP, say, for boy

indicators.note: the word for again lets the doctor in, so it wraps round those letters

parts.note: anew means again
a GP, a family doctor, is an example of a Dr

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going back to the family doctor with their son.
explanation.walkthrough: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew is a common boy's name.

clue.text: Relax amid weapons that may be dropped between seats

definitions.text: that may be dropped between seats

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the word for relax sits inside the weapons

parts.note: arms are weapons
to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: Laying down arms between seats in an orderly ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that may be dropped between seats' is a descriptive definition: the folding elbow rest between two seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Supports for the elbow, often folding down between adjacent seats in cinemas, cars or planes.

clue.text: Journalist often has this problem with broadband?

definitions.meaning: reporters constantly face a time limit for filing their copy
a connection that has stopped working, a phone cable gone silent

explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the answer describes a broadband connection that has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: The time by which copy must be filed, a constant pressure for reporters, and also a broken connection.

clue.text: Practises to miss out one man in the middle, going over football move

indicators.note: to miss something out is to omit it, so the one is removed

parts.note: trains means practises
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: going over means turning back, so the official is read backwards

parts.note: the referee is the official in the middle of a game

explanation.surface: A footballer misses training and the referee goes over a deal for the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to miss out' drops I from TRAINS; 'going over' turns REF to FER.
explanation.definitionFit: A player's move from one football club to another is the usual name for this deal.

clue.text: A bishop merged with competitor for Advent

indicators.note: merged with means the two pieces overlap, sharing the letter where they meet, so one copy drops

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop
a rival is a competitor

explanation.surface: A bishop amalgamated with a rival diocese in time for Advent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merged with' overlaps RR and RIVAL, sharing one R, so A + RR + RIVAL becomes A R RIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means a coming or arrival, as of Christ; capitalised here only to suggest the church season.

clue.text: Right to support the monarch

parts.note: to prop is to support
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's cipher

explanation.surface: It is right to support the monarch, as a loyal subject would say.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and fitting, as in the right or appropriate way to behave.

clue.text: No epicure having Indian bread before function

indicators.note: the bread comes before the function in the answer

parts.note: puri is a deep-fried Indian bread
tan is the tangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Someone who is no gourmet eats Indian bread before a formal function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' is not a party but the maths tangent, TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict, austere person who shuns pleasure, unlike a lover of fine food.

clue.text: Corrupt one imprisoned that may be pardoned

indicators.note: a prisoner is held inside, so the one sits within the corrupt word

parts.note: venal means corrupt, open to bribery
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A crooked prisoner who may receive a pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' puts I inside VENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied to a sin, it means minor and forgivable, as opposed to mortal.

clue.text: With best intentions, take a reading additionally

parts.note: doing something with good intent is doing it for a worthy purpose
to measure is to take a reading on a gauge

explanation.surface: Someone well-meaning takes an extra gauge reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning as an extra, beyond what is strictly needed.

clue.text: Raise very old statue

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word means writing it upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: sore was once used to mean very, as in the biblical 'sore afraid'

explanation.surface: An instruction to put up an ancient statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' reverses SORE. Eros is the well-known statue at Piccadilly Circus in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous winged statue at Piccadilly Circus in London is popularly called by this name.

clue.text: Historian left one going up the wall

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant that grows up walls

explanation.surface: A historian leaves, someone driven up the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up the wall' suggests being driven mad; here it describes a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Livy was the Roman historian who wrote a vast history of Rome.

clue.text: I may take vehicle through traffic light in attempt to obstruct legal passage

indicators.note: taking the vehicle through the light puts it within the light's word

parts.note: a filter is a green arrow on a traffic light allowing one lane to turn
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A driver takes a vehicle through a traffic light, meanwhile a bill is stalled.
explanation.walkthrough: A filter is the green arrow on a British traffic light letting one lane turn while the rest wait.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon speech made to delay or block the passing of a bill in a legislature.

clue.text: Colour seen in large part to be very loud

indicators.note: only a large part of the colour word is used, so its last two letters are lost

parts.note: yellow is a colour

explanation.surface: A colour, seen over much of the area, is very loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in large part' cuts YELLOW to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout, to be extremely loud in voice.

clue.text: Actual score halved — wrong returns in game

parts.note: real means actual
a score is twenty, so half of it is ten

indicators.note: a word that returns goes back the way it came, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A tennis scoreline is actually halved after a wrong call is overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns SIN to NIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The original indoor form of tennis, played in a walled court, as at Hampton Court.
